sections.content: How many people are "forestry and related workers"?

5,760 people

were counted on the census as "forestry and related workers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Forestry workers carry out tasks related to the planting, cultivation and protection of trees.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "forestry and related workers" there were more men than women (92.2% compared with 7.8%).

This means "forestry and related workers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary trades and related occupations".

Men made up 92.2% and women made up 7.8% of "forestry and related workers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "forestry and related workers" included:

  • marine and waterways transport operatives
  • aerospace engineers
  • IT network professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "forestry and related workers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "forestry and related workers", 12.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "forestry and related workers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "forestry and related workers" included:

  • receptionists
  • marine and waterways transport operatives
  • precision instrument makers and repairers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "forestry and related workers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "forestry and related workers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "forestry and related workers", 9.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (78.9% compared with 21.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (58.5%) than self-employed (41.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Northumberland, this is in the region of the North East.
